root_cause.text: The s390 syscall dispatcher lacked a Spectre v1 mitigation boundary, allowing a speculatively executed out-of-bounds array access on the syscall function pointer table when userspace provides an invalid syscall number.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `#include <linux/nospec.h>` and inserts `nr = array_index_nospec(nr, NR_syscalls);` immediately before the `sys_call_table[nr]` dereference. This mitigates Spectre v1 by preventing speculative execution from accessing syscall function pointers beyond the valid table bounds. The vulnerability exists because the syscall number `nr` is directly controlled by userspace (via CPU registers) and was previously used to index into `sys_call_table` without any speculative execution barrier, even though a bounds check (`if (likely(nr < NR_syscalls))`) was present—bounds checks alone do not prevent speculative out-of-bounds memory reads on vulnerable CPUs.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add nospec header inclusion to enable speculative execution vulnerability protections in this kernel module.
intent_record.what: Added `#include <linux/nospec.h>` header file after the existing `#include <linux/cpufeature.h>` line in the include section.
intent_record.how: This makes the nospec (no speculative execution) kernel API available to this compilation unit, enabling use of speculation barrier macros and functions (such as barrier_nospec()) that protect against speculative execution vulnerabilities like Spectre.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add Spectre v1 mitigation to the syscall dispatch path by using array_index_nospec() to prevent speculative out-of-bounds syscall table access.
intent_record.what: Added braces around the conditional block and inserted a call to `array_index_nospec(nr, NR_syscalls)` before the syscall table lookup, assigning the result back to `nr`.
intent_record.how: This change mitigates Spectre v1 attacks by preventing speculative execution from accessing the syscall table out-of-bounds. The `array_index_nospec()` function ensures that even if the CPU speculates past the bounds check, the index is clamped to valid range before being used to dereference `sys_call_table[nr]`, preventing information leakage through cache side-channels.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit shows a critical change to the syscall dispatcher boundary check. The original code had `if (likely(nr < NR_syscalls))` which performs an unsafe bounds check vulnerable to Spectre v1 - the CPU could speculatively execute the array access even when nr is out of bounds. The fixed code changes this to `if (likely(nr >= NR_syscalls)) goto out;` which inverts the logic to check for the invalid case first and exit early, preventing speculative execution of the out-of-bounds array access on `current->thread.sys_call_table[nr]`. This is a proper Spectre v1 mitigation boundary that prevents the vulnerable speculative path from reaching the array dereference. The vulnerable construct (unsafe bounds check before array access) is ABSENT in this version - it has already been corrected.
